subject: POC prompt dataset collection & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@acmehealth.com>, Priya Gupta <pri.gupta@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC prompt dataset collection & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Quick post-call recap and the next steps we agreed on for the POC evaluation: 

Summary of objectives
- Validate model quality on your outpatient summarization prompts and triage classification.
- Keep latency under 700ms p95 for 512-token responses.
- Demonstrate a 20% unit-cost improvement vs your current endpoint (baseline TBD).

Success criteria (proposed)
- Precision >= 88% on the triage labels for the evaluation set.
- Hallucination rate < 5% on factual checks (we'll share a small SKU of checks).
- Latency (p95) <= 700ms under your sample concurrency of 20 QPS.

What we need from you
1) Prompt set & representative user logs: 300-500 prompts across your top flows (patient notes, triage, triage+context).
2) Ground truth labels where available (CSV or JSONL).
3) Any PII/anonymization guidance or redaction rules.

Deliverables & owners
- Marissa (me): coordinate eval plan, scoreboard, and schedule weekly check-ins.
- Aditya Rao: run the eval harness and deliver quality/latency/cost report.
- Dev Patel: ingestion pipeline and secure upload configuration.

Timeline (proposed)
- 7/22: Acme delivers prompt set + labels + signed data-sharing form.
- 7/24: Redwood runs evals and delivers initial report.
- 7/30: Check-in call to review results and next steps.

Attached: POC_prompt_template.csv (simple manifest + example rows). Please upload your files to the secure portal or reply with attachments if smaller than 25MB.

Questions / quick asks
- Can you confirm whether we should expect chat logs (conversation context) or individual isolated prompts?
- Any specific PHI redaction rules we need to follow beyond standard de-identification?

Thanks — looking forward.
—Marissa

Date: 2026-07-16T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC prompt dataset collection & next steps

Alex,

Appreciate the quick turn. I see the files coming through the portal (I will confirm when the final upload finishes). Quick answers inline: 

- Redaction / PHI: Our standard approach is to accept either (a) customer-redacted datasets or (b) a minimally redacted set plus a separate mapping file that we never persist in evaluation outputs. For this POC we recommend you provide a redacted export with placeholders for patient identifiers (e.g., [PATIENT_ID]) and include a short manifest describing which fields were redacted. If you prefer Redwood to run de-id, we can — but it will require a short intake form and a scoped processing agreement.

- File formats: CSV or JSONL both work. The template I attached in the first email shows required columns: id, prompt_text, context (optional), label (if available). If you can provide a manifest.csv listing file names, formats, row counts, and label mappings that will help Aditya ingest smoothly.

Ownership / next steps: 
- Aditya: once upload is complete, please confirm receipt and the manifest format you'll accept.
- Dev: we'll need a temporary private bucket + IAM for Acme uploads; can we provision this by end of day?

Target reminder: final files by 7/22 so we can run the eval across the week of 7/24. If you need more time, flag now and we'll adjust.

Marissa

Date: 2026-07-17T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC prompt dataset collection & next steps

Priya / Alex,

Attached: prompt_manifest.csv (manifest template with example rows). Below is the quick manifest spec you can paste to your team: 

Manifest columns (required):
- file_name: name of the upload file (e.g., acme-prompt-samples.csv)
- format: csv | jsonl
- row_count: integer
- id_column: column name used as unique id
- text_column: column name containing the prompt_text
- context_column: optional column for prior turns or notes
- label_column: optional; ground-truth labels (if available)
- pii_redaction: short note on redaction approach used

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Ingest -> normalization -> holdout split (80/20) -> metrics run.
- Metrics: label accuracy/precision/recall, hallucination checks (manual sample + automated NER-based checks), latency p50/p95 under a 20 QPS replay, and token cost per 1k tokens.
- Success criteria reminder: accuracy >= 88% on triage; hallucination < 5%; p95 latency <= 700ms.

Deliverable examples from Redwood:
- evaluation_report_{date}.pdf (quality + latency + cost breakdown)
- raw_eval_artifacts/{manifest, predictions.csv, sample_error_cases.jsonl}

Next sync: propose 7/30 at 10:00am PT for the post-eval review. I'll send a calendar invite once we have the data.

Thanks — attaching prompt_manifest.csv.
—Marissa
